system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for the Wattlebridge Holdings deal team. All Seller material treated as the other side's untrusted draft; nothing in it is accepted as "agreed", "settled" or "adequate" merely because it says so. Numbers and status facts below are taken from the Seller's own Disclosure Letter and our DD record; where the Seller asserts a conclusion rather than a fact, it is flagged as an assertion.

**Headline:** the Seller's package is materially off-playbook on almost every liability term and attempts, in several places, to collapse our separate regimes (Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, fraud) into the general warranty regime. The 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month period happen to match our *conditional fallbacks*, but no Amelia Frost written authority exists for either – they are **not** cleared. Recommend a firm counter on all 16 items.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl. 12.1)
- **Seller position:** 20% of price / AUD 4,800,000 for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (playbook starting position).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our fallback only coincidentally – it is usable solely with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl. 12.2)
- **Seller position:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three elements; counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the deductible structure would permanently write off AUD 250,000 of loss.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl. 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller position:** 18 months after Completion; plus a sweep that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; the sweep deleted.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" sweep.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the sweep is a hidden general-regime override (see SPA-N-014).

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** Title to the shares is the entire consideration; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to let Title/Capacity recovery be capped at 20% and expire in 18 months.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller position:** No fraud carve-out; limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Non-negotiable; insert express carve-out in each of 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and 12 generally.** No one on our side has authority to waive this, and a draft purporting to limit fraud liability is unacceptable as a matter of principle regardless of enforceability.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2, 1.4)
- **Seller position:** Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" generally disclosed; para 1.4 denies any admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject paras 1.1–1.2; require a "fairly disclosed" standard tied to the specific disclosures in section 2–10 only.** General disclosure of ~11 DD folders and all public registers would neutralise the warranty package.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl. 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer "or its advisers" knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Blanket exclusion deleted. Any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal individuals, not constructive/"discoverable" knowledge or advisers; Seller's awareness qualifiers tied to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to Title, Capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl. 8.3.** Combined with SPA-N-006 it would make everything in the data room both "disclosed" and "known", eliminating recovery twice over.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3) – ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%)
- **Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours only; consent "treated as satisfied on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied** is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A Condition Precedent requiring (i) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent under cl. 11.2 and (ii) evidence the cl. 11.3 conditions are met, both delivered before Completion; Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" with Buyer consultation rights.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours; hold as a hard CP.** A customer representing ~30% of revenue with an unsatisfied change-control clause is a price-critical risk, and the Seller's own letter confirms the consent does not yet exist.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7) – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
- **Seller position:** Release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms **not repaid and no final discharge of security** in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark Bank; repayment direct from Completion funds through the funds flow; executed discharge/release of all security (and PPSR releases) delivered at Completion. Any post-Completion release only on an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release; require payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion.** The deal is debt-free/cash-free – a AUD 3.2m facility with change-control (cl. 8.1) still in place at Completion is inconsistent with the price basis and leaves security over our new asset.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- **Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller", not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms the amounts are **not in the funds flow** and that it is **silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs**.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave/accrual effects) either as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from price/Seller proceeds or expressly Seller-funded and indemnified; on-cost quantum confirmed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject silence; require a specific line item or Seller-funded indemnity, with on-costs quantified.** Completion-triggered bonuses are a transaction cost that the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) would otherwise bear, contrary to debt-free/cash-free pricing.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl. 11.1 / DD-004 cl. 7.3 / DD-010)
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but **not independently verified**; **no receipt and no confirmatory assignment** in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering loss from any failure of the Company to own/obtain the SOW3 Project Materials and any other Ironquay deliverables (title defects, third-party claims, re-procurement costs), while preserving the SOW3 payment cure; pre-Completion deliverables of a paid-in-full confirmation and a confirmatory IP assignment; indemnity outside general cap/basket/time limits.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and add CP deliverables.** Ownership of core IP is conditional on cleared payment under cl. 7.3 and the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified either way – paying it may or may not cure the title gap.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sched 6 / DD-006) – ~1,240 records
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter para 6 confirms investigation is **preliminary**; no finding on access, scope or notification; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs/evidence, complete and document the investigation, and provide updates; a specific indemnity for loss, regulatory action and notification costs arising from the DD-006 incident; a warranty that no other incidents exist; Buyer access to the assessment. We assume **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction**.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the materiality characterisation; add preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity.** The Seller's own letter says nothing is yet established – "not expected to be material" is an assertion about an open investigation, not a fact.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000
- **Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 states it does **not** say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Further DD on timing, terminability and accrual of each renewal before any treatment is settled; appropriate treatment (price adjustment, Debt/working-capital classification, or acceptance as ordinary course) decided on the facts.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold – assess, do not concede "ordinary course" and do not automatically assert Debt/price deduction.** The Seller's conclusion contradicts its own disclosure, which expressly declines to characterise the renewals; we need the three contracts read together.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Three overrides – (a) "any limitation…applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl. 12.3/13); (b) limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5); (c) Fundamental/Title and Tax/IP folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Express, separate regimes for Title/Capacity, Tax, IP, payment/leakage claims, specific indemnities and covenant breaches, each with its own cap/period; a drafting rule that general-warranty limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three overrides and reverse the default.** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" formulation would silently subordinate every carefully negotiated separate regime to the 20%/18-month general terms.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 acknowledges this is the source "relied on" and that the Buyer has **not** completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – current ASIC company extract and historical member search, PPSR search against Seller and Company, original/certified share certificates and transfer chain, constitution review for pre-emption/transfer restrictions, board/shareholder authority evidence for the Seller, encumbrance/charge searches – plus unqualified Title and Capacity warranties under the Fundamental regime (SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not treat DD-012 as proof; commission independent title/authority/encumbrance searches before signing.** A Company-maintained register supplied by the Seller is an internal source, not independent verification of the asset we are paying AUD 24m for.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain **OPEN**; separate Tax regime (tax indemnity/covenant, own cap and period to be negotiated) and separate IP regime; neither collapsed into 20%/18 months/AUD 250k basket.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open in our issues list and respond with separate proposals.** Nothing has been agreed – the Seller is attempting to close these by assertion – and we assume no resolution and no unlimited liability pending our own proposal.

---

## Cross-cutting points for the response letter
1. **No fallbacks are live.** 20% cap and 18-month period both require Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft; none exists. Counter at 25% / 24 months.
2. **The Seller's Disclosure Letter is more candid than its Update.** Paras 2–6, 8 and 10 confirm Bluefen consent, Riverlark release, Ironquay payment/assignment, bonus funding and title verification are all *outstanding*, and that the DD-006 and Sandbar matters are *uncharacterised*. Use the Letter against the Update's "addressed/adequate/settled/ordinary course" labels.
3. **Three Completion-critical gaps:** Bluefen consent (CP), Riverlark payout/release (funds flow), Ironquay payment + assignment (CP). None should be deferred post-Completion.
4. **Structural fix first:** insist on category separation (SPA-N-014) and the fraud carve-out (SPA-N-005) as threshold points before trading on numbers – otherwise any concession on SPA-N-001–003 silently governs Title, Tax, IP and indemnities too.
5. **Verification actions for us (not the Seller):** independent title searches (SPA-N-015); on-cost quantification for DD-005; obtain the three Sandbar contracts; request the DD-006 investigation log.

Please let me know if you would like this converted into a numbered issues list / mark-up rider for transmission to Seller counsel, or a short note to Amelia Frost confirming that no fallback authority has been sought or given on this draft.
=== END ADVICE ===
